macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street slips as investors await U.S. inflation data and Fed-rate signals
items.summary: U.S. stocks edged lower, with the Dow down 0.11%, the S&P 500 down 0.06%, and the Nasdaq down 0.32% as traders focused on upcoming July inflation figures that could shape Federal Reserve expectations. Treasury yields also rose, with the 10-year note up to 4.701%, while the dollar strengthened modestly.

items.title: Oil prices rally on Strait of Hormuz risk, pressuring broader markets
items.summary: Oil prices jumped about 5% as markets monitored tensions tied to the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to a cautious tone in equities. The move came alongside a stronger U.S. dollar and higher Treasury yields.

items.title: U.S. labor market weakens as July payrolls report shows job losses
items.summary: The U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, according to the latest jobs report, adding to concerns about a cooling labor market. The weaker data has intensified attention on inflation, consumer spending, and the Federal Reserve's next move.

items.title: Markets trim odds of an imminent Fed rate hike after recent data
items.summary: Markets are now pricing in a lower chance of a September rate increase, with one market snapshot citing about a 44% probability, down sharply from 67% a week earlier. Investors are awaiting the next inflation reading for clues on whether the Fed will tighten further.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty weaken in India as mid- and small-caps outperform
items.summary: Indian equities finished lower, with the Sensex down 388 points and the Nifty slipping below 24,500, while mid-cap and small-cap stocks outperformed. The move reflects a mixed risk tone in regional markets.

items.title: RBI rate-cut expectations shift as inflation outlook stays subdued
items.summary: Economists now expect the Reserve Bank of India may raise rates in December or later, reflecting lower core inflation and the central bank's decision to keep rates unchanged while cutting its inflation forecast. Overnight indexed swap markets also point to fewer hikes over the next year.

items.title: Supreme Court tariff ruling prompts U.S. refund of about $100 billion
items.summary: The Trump administration is moving to refund roughly $100 billion in tariffs after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down many of the levies earlier this year. The decision is one of the most significant recent trade-policy developments affecting markets and businesses.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $64K as macro and geopolitical risk pressures crypto
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around the low-$64,000 area and briefly slipped below $64,000 as traders weighed U.S.-Iran tensions, Hormuz-related uncertainty, and broader risk-off sentiment. Ether, XRP, Solana, and Cardano also fell, with one market report noting more than $200 million in liquidations over the prior 24 hours.

items.title: Bitcoin price falls 1.38% to around $64,072
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to roughly $63,754 before recovering to about $64,072, marking a 1.38% decline over 24 hours. The move was attributed to macro uncertainty and fresh volatility in crypto markets.

items.title: Coinbase launches crypto derivatives in the UK with leverage up to 50x
items.summary: Coinbase reportedly rolled out more than 170 crypto derivatives contracts in the UK for eligible professional investors, including perpetuals and futures with leverage up to 50x. The expansion marks a significant product development in a major regulated market.

items.title: South Korea scraps the 1 million won crypto Travel Rule threshold
items.summary: South Korea moved to remove the 1 million won threshold for applying the Travel Rule to crypto transfers, tightening compliance expectations for exchanges and users. The change is a notable regulatory development in one of Asia's most active crypto markets.

items.title: SEC schedules Aug. 14 meeting on crypto offering rules
items.summary: The SEC set a meeting for Aug. 14 to discuss rules related to crypto offerings, signaling continued regulatory attention in the U.S. The agenda suggests policy discussions remain active even amid broader market volatility.

items.title: MiCA deadline leaves 1,062 EEA crypto firms without authorization
items.summary: A report said 1,062 crypto firms in the EEA remained without authorization as the MiCA deadline passed, highlighting the scale of compliance pressure under the EU's new framework. The development underscores how regulatory transition continues to reshape the European crypto industry.

items.title: Broadridge processes $8 trillion in July through blockchain repo platform
items.summary: Broadridge said it processed $8 trillion in July via its blockchain-based repo platform, a notable sign of continued institutional blockchain adoption. The figure points to significant usage in capital markets infrastructure rather than retail crypto trading.

items.title: XRP bridge loses 200,000 XRP after relayer logic flaw
items.summary: A bridge tied to XRP reportedly lost 200,000 XRP due to a relayer logic flaw, adding to concerns about cross-chain security. The incident is another reminder that bridge infrastructure remains a frequent target for exploits and operational failures.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Valve warns EU Steam hardware customers their personal data may have been compromised
items.summary: Valve told Steam hardware customers in Europe that their personal data was likely affected after a cyberattack on logistics provider CEVA Logistics, which ships Steam hardware in Europe. The notice also warned customers to expect possible fake messages following the incident.

items.title: Halloween: The Game banned in Australia and New Zealand
items.summary: IllFonic’s Halloween game has been denied a rating in Australia and New Zealand because players can smoke weed in it, effectively blocking release in those markets. The studio said the refusal was tied to the presence of a controlled substance.

items.title: New free Quake campaign released for the 30th anniversary
items.summary: MachineGames has released a new free Quake campaign to mark the franchise’s 30th anniversary. The release adds fresh content to the classic shooter and is available now.

items.title: SanDisk launches new Xbox Series X/S expansion cards
items.summary: SanDisk has become the third company to offer Xbox Series X/S expansion cards, with a 2TB model priced at $340. The company’s listing suggests pricing could rise further.

items.title: THQ Nordic says 12 unannounced games are in development
items.summary: THQ Nordic said it currently has 29 games in development, including 12 that have not yet been revealed. The publisher has disclosed 17 of those projects so far.

items.title: Evercade announces Doom Collection with new gameplay modifiers
items.summary: Evercade unveiled a Doom Collection containing eight campaigns along with Evercade-exclusive gameplay modifiers. The package expands the retro platform’s licensed catalog.

items.title: Knytt Classic gets free 20th anniversary release on Steam
items.summary: The indie game Knytt has received a 20th anniversary version for modern PCs. The new Knytt Classic is available now for free on Steam.

items.title: Hello Games marks No Man’s Sky’s 10th anniversary
items.summary: Hello Games CEO Sean Murray thanked players for supporting No Man’s Sky on its 10th anniversary. He noted that players have still discovered less than 1% of the game’s planets.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Rebirth follow-up gets a new look at Gamescom Opening Night Live
items.summary: A new look at the next Final Fantasy VII project, hosted by its director, is set for Gamescom’s Opening Night Live. The teaser positions the game for another major public reveal.

items.title: GameStop may have damaged some Nintendo Switch 2 pre-orders
items.summary: Some customers are reporting that GameStop may have damaged Nintendo Switch 2 units tied to pre-orders. The issue has triggered complaints from buyers awaiting launch deliveries.
